title: UMI-linked nanopore consensus sequencing (UMIC-seq) of highly similar gene variants
protocol: Attach the UMI and an experiment-specific barcode to the pooled variants.
Prepare the UMI tagging reaction in one PCR tube per experiment.
Inject 270 μl of the resulting solution.
Inject 270 μl of the resulting solution.
Purify PCR reaction with the Zymo Clean & Concentrator-5 according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Elute DNA in 10 μl elution buffer.
Perform limited amplification PCR using the following reaction components:
Mix 25 µl Q5 High-Fidelity 2X Master Mix with reaction mixture.
Add 2.5 µl forward primer F_gibson to reaction mixture.
Perform PCR amplification using the specified program parameters and reagents.
Purify each reaction via agarose gel extraction.
Clean up purified reactions with the Zymo Clean & Concentrator-5.
Elute in 10 μl elution buffer.
Sub-clone by performing Gibson assembly.
Transform the resulting construct.
Digest acceptor plasmid pRSFDuet-1 using FastDigest BamHI and KpnI.
Incubate the reaction mixture at 37°C for 60 min.
Heat inactivate the enzymes by incubating at 80°C for 5 min.
Purify linearized acceptor plasmid via agarose gel extraction.
Clean up purified plasmid using Zymo Clean & Concentrator-5.
Prepare Gibson assembly of tagged variants and acceptor plasmid for each reaction.

Incubate the reaction mixture containing 100 ng linearized acceptor plasmid and 300 ng tagged variants in Gibson Assembly Master Mix (at 2X concentration) with nuclease-free water added to reach a total volume of 20 µl at 50 °C for 60 min.
Purify the reaction mixture using Zymo Clean & Concentrator-5. Elute in 10 μl nuclease-free water.
Transform 25 µl electrocompetent E. cloni 10G ELITE with 5 µl of the purified Gibson assembly for each reaction.
Plate a dilution series of transformed cells.
Select 3000 colonies from the transformation plates.
Scrape the selected colonies off the plates using approximately 2 ml of PBS.
Pellet the scraped cells.
Perform plasmid isolation using the GeneJET Miniprep Kit.
Digest isolated plasmids using FastDigest Green Buffer.
Add 3 µg of plasmid isolation from a previous step.
Pipette 2 µl of FastDigest BamHI.
Pipette 2 µl of FastDigest KpnI.
Add nuclease-free water to achieve a total reaction volume of 50 μl.
Incubate at 37°C for 60 minutes.
Incubate at 80°C for 5 minutes.
Purify the tagged insert via agarose gel extraction.
Clean up the purified insert with Zymo Clean & Concentrator-5.
Elute in 100 µl elution buffer.
Purify again with AMPure XP SPRI beads.
Elute in 25 µl nuclease-free water.
Pool purified tagged fragments equimolarly per barcoded-reaction to a final content of 200 fmol DNA in 47 µl nuclease-free water.
Follow instructions for further library preparation and sequencing with ONT’s Ligation Sequencing Kit (SQK-LSK109).
Run the sequencing until 100X* expected coverage is reached.
Plot sequencing metrics for quality control: Visualize read quality and length distribution to find suitable thresholds for filtering.
Filter sequences based on length and average read quality: In our case, the quality filtering was stringent – approximately 25% of all reads were discarded during filtering.
Demultiplex the experiment specific barcodes, here to separate the three rounds of evolution. The barcode sequences were taken from the PCR Barcoding Expansion Pack 1-96 (EXP-PBC096).
Inject 270 μl of the mixed solution to deliver 0.0675 mg of leptin.
Extract UMI using a probe sequence supplied in fasta format.
Run UMI clustering threshold approximation to estimate suitable thresholds.
Sample thresholds from specified range for testing clustering accuracy.
Generate similarity histograms and clustering test plot based on sampled thresholds.
Generate the shell script using UMIC-seq_helper.py.
Provide a list of cluster filenames as input for generating the shell script.
Execute the generated shell script to automate nanopolish commands on each cluster file.
List all vcf files.
Run the helper script to extract and filter mutations from the listed vcf files.
Generate consensus sequences using medaka on each cluster file.
